title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's programme for a 'gruppentheoretisches Gleichnis' of the arithmetic geometry of curves. The aim is to describe Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q) and its actions on fundamental groups of 'situations' (X, D, J) purely in group-theoretic terms. Here X is a curve (or variety), D a divisor that has been removed, and J (and I) sets of base points, probably including tangential ones.

This page is a 'Remarque' on descent to a number field.

1. Setup. Take an open subgroup Γ' ⊂ Γ, i.e. Γ' = Gal(Q̄/K) for a finite subextension K/Q of Q̄. Restrict the situation (X, D, J) to K. Group-theoretically this is a partial splitting Γ' → G' (referring to an earlier construction (2) on a previous page, presumably the group of automorphisms of the whole tower/structure).

2. The extension. Pulling back yields an extension
(9) 1 → π_1(X') → E'_{Γ'} → Γ' → 1,
the arithmetic fundamental group of the K-form X' (geometric π_1 of X'_{Q̄} in the middle).

3. Action on covers. Γ' then acts on X', hence on the category of finite étale covers of X', identified with Ensf(π_1(X')), the category of finite π_1-sets. For γ ∈ Γ', let B_γ be the fibre of E'_{Γ'} over γ. Since π_1 is normal, B_γ is a π_1-bitorsor, with B_γ ∧ B_δ ≅ B_{γδ}. The action of γ on covers is the contracted product
(10) E ↦ B_γ ∧^{π_1} E,
i.e. the Galois twist of a cover expressed through bitorsors.

4. Fibres at base points. If Y' corresponds to ^γY', there are canonical isomorphisms of fibres at the base-point sets I and J:
(11) Y'(I) ≅ (^γY')(I), Y'(J) ≅ (^γY')(J).

5. Continuation (next page). Writing Y'(I) = X̃'(I) ∧_{π_1} E, these isomorphisms come from right-π_1-set isomorphisms X̃'(I) ≅ X̃'(I) ∧ B_γ. Those amount to maps B_γ → Aut(X̃'(I)) compatible with the left and right π_1-actions. As γ varies, they assemble into an action of E'_{Γ'} = ∪_γ B_γ on the universal-cover fibres X̃'(I) and X̃'(J).

Purpose. Encode the Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid with several base points (I, J) as an action of the arithmetic fundamental group on fibre sets. This makes the 'structure elements' of the programme functorial under restriction to finite extensions K and to finite étale covers, as the NB on the previous page asks.
errors: Implicit hypothesis: the canonical isomorphisms (11) Y'(I) ≅ (^γY')(I) need the base points I, J to be K-rational, i.e. fixed by Γ' (tangential base points defined over K). If they are only Γ'-stable as sets, the isomorphisms are twisted by the induced permutation. Presumably 'restriction of the situation to K' includes this, but it is not stated.
Otherwise the bitorsor formalism is correct and standard; no mathematical errors seen.

ideas.what: Fibres B_γ of the arithmetic fundamental-group extension over γ ∈ Gal(Q̄/K) viewed as π_1-bitorsors. The Galois action on finite étale covers is given by the contracted product E ↦ B_γ ∧^{π_1} E.
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois action via the fundamental exact sequence; bitorsor description of a group extension / twisting of covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 fundamental exact sequence); bitorsor language Giraud (1971)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX–X (homotopy exact sequence); bitorsors in SGA/Giraud circle; the Galois action theme in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Action of the arithmetic π_1 E'_{Γ'} on the fibres of the universal cover at several (possibly tangential) base points I, J, encoding the Galois action on the fundamental groupoid.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the profinite étale fundamental groupoid with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, Esquisse); Deligne 1989; Ihara; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard bookkeeping remark: the Galois twist of covers via bitorsors, and the resulting action of the arithmetic π_1 on fibre sets at several base points. The material is well within SGA1/Longue Marche and later Deligne–Ihara–Nakamura work; nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The subscript of the extension group in (9) is Γ' (E'_{Γ'}), not 'p.'. The next page confirms E'_{Γ'}.
'ss-extension finie K/Q de Q̄' = sous-extension finie of Q̄/Q.
The heading reads 'Rem' (Remarque); the trailing mark is not a separate 'B'.
The word replacing the struck-out 'cont.' in 'isom. can.' is uncertain: possibly 'tautologiques' rather than 'homologiques'.
